key_insight: Nd and Ce do segregate to grain boundaries in TiN, but unlike in bcc Fe they usually do not strongly weaken the boundary, so TiN better retains grain-boundary strength under fission-product exposure.
engineering_relevance: This supports TiN and related nitride coatings as more damage-tolerant FCCI barriers, with grain-boundary strength retention serving as a useful metric for corrosion-cracking susceptibility.
method: First-principles segregation calculations for Nd and Ce at six coincident-site lattice grain boundaries in bcc Fe and TiN.
Work-of-separation and traction-separation analyses to assess cleavage resistance and ideal crack-opening strength.
Bonding analysis to identify how segregation alters local interfacial chemistry and load-bearing bonds.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated grain boundaries, Nd/Ce segregation was favorable in both materials, but median work-of-separation and peak-traction retentions were much higher in TiN than in Fe, indicating far less mechanical degradation.
watch_item: The results are atomistic and boundary-specific, so real coating performance will still depend on microstructure, defect density, temperature, irradiation, and chemical environment.
paper_title: Grain boundary strength and corrosion cracking susceptibility in TiN coatings under fission product segregation
